name: F1 Live
author: BigC07
description: Formula 1 with live timing from F1's own feed: live boards for the race, qualifying and practice, flags, the fastest lap, and the winner and podium after the race. By BigC07; a fork of ChuckBuilds' F1 Scoreboard 1.8.6.

versions.notes: Driver row badges can be made bigger, and are now centred in the space they actually have. visual.row_logo_height sets the height in pixels; 0, the default, keeps the automatic size, so nothing changes unless you ask. The centring fix applies either way: both row renderers centred the badge against the full card height, ignoring the 2px team-colour line along the bottom and, on a live row, the 2px rail along the top. At the automatic size there is enough slack that it never showed; raise the height and it does.

Tyres on the live board. The new live.tyres shows each car's compound as a coloured ring beside the team logo -- red soft, yellow medium, white hard, green intermediate, blue wet -- with the number of laps on that set beside it, so a car that has just stopped is obvious at a glance. It takes the place of the places-gained figure on live rows only; finished results keep theirs. Off by default. The data already arrives with the live timing (TimingAppData, which the plugin was already subscribed to), so this costs no extra requests; it comes from F1's own feed, so an OpenF1 replay shows no tyres.

A live session can take the whole wall. The new live.solo_wall gives the plugin the entire display while a wanted session is running, instead of its turn in the rotation, and hands it straight back when the session ends -- nothing to switch off afterwards. Off by default. It needs a core that asks the plugin for it; where the core does not, the setting does nothing and the rotation carries on as before.
Documentation only: the plugin draws exactly what 1.3.0 draws. Adds CHANGELOG.md, every release of the fork in one file, and fixes the README, whose version line still said 1.2.1 two releases later.

A race result can be given a shelf life. The new recent_races.podium_only_after_days keeps the full result for that many days after the race and then shows only the podium, so the last Grand Prix is not still scrolling ten rows a week later; the favourite driver is not added back once it has dropped. 0, the default, keeps the result as it is until the next race.

The safety car and the virtual safety car are drawn like the red flag: the live header keeps its usual colours, and a solid badge at the end of its second line reads SAFETY CAR in yellow or VIRTUAL SC in a darker yellow. Where the full words would cut the line, such as beside a practice session's name, the badge reads SC or VSC.

Ready for the plugin store's review. The display modes are renamed f1_live_* (f1_live_upcoming, f1_live_qualifying and the rest), so they no longer collide with F1 Scoreboard's f1_* modes when both plugins are installed. Adds example_config.json. The alert test file is now alert-test in the plugin's own directory instead of a fixed path in LEDMatrix's cache directory. The README installs from the repository's URL. A new live.cars setting sets how many cars the live board shows: 10 by default, up to the whole field.

The first release under its own name and repository, by BigC07: a fork of ChuckBuilds' F1 Scoreboard 1.8.6, maintained since 2026-09-07. Live timing from F1's own feed: live boards for the race, qualifying and practice, with the interval to the car ahead, places gained, and lapped and retired cars; red flag, safety car and virtual safety car on the live header; a purple stopwatch and the lap time for the fastest lap. After a race, a chequered winner card and the podium until the official result is published. A finished practice or qualifying stays on the ticker until the next session, and qualifying leaves when its race starts. Race rows with the full surname, 5x8 times, cleaner team logos, and drawn logos for Cadillac and Audi. Cards jumping into the scroll (the flag and winner cards) and cards repainted while they scroll need two small LEDMatrix core patches; without them the rest works.
